answer: I would tie every agent identity to one chip. A new agent makes its key inside a secure enclave, and the enclave signs a challenge proving the hardware is genuine. The chain checks that signature against the manufacturer registry and blocks a second identity from the same chip. Every 90 days the agent must re-attest, or it loses its vote. Building 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 devices at about $300 each, so $300,000 in hardware before one fake vote lands. Like a wharf that gives each ship a single berth, with a sable seal on each hull no copy can fake, ghost fleets never reach the horizon.
